Fourth seed Elena Dementieva avoided an embarrassing early exit when comeback queen Jelena Dokic's French Open hopes were ended by a back injury on Thursday. Jelena Dokic was left in tears after being forced to retire hurt against Elena Dementieva at the French Open. Dokic, taking part in her first French Open since 2004 following well-documented family problems, won the first set 6-2 and -- after her first break for treatment -- broke the 2004 finalist to lead 3-2 in their second round clash. But the Russian won the next two games as the tearful former world No.4 was reduced to walking pace before calling it quits. "I went for a return and I just went down and couldn't get back up," she said. "It's very painful and very disappointing because I felt as if I had the match in my hands." Dokic, now ranked 80th after reviving her career with a run to the quarter-finals of the Australian Open in January, had won her opening match on Tuesday when she came back from a set down to beat Slovenia's Karolina Sprem 3-6 6-1 6-2. The 26-year-old's career had nosedived following her highly-publicized split from controversial mentor and father Damir. Dementieva will next play Australian 30th seed Samantha Stosur, who won her second-round match in straight sets against Belgium's Yanina Wickmayer. Earlier on Thursday, the Williams sisters also progressed through to the third round with contrasting victories. Second seed Serena crushed Virginia Ruano Pascual 6-2 6-0 to set up a clash with another unseeded Spaniard, Maria Jose Martinez Sanchez. Third seed Venus survived a scare against unseeded Czech Lucie Safarova before completing a match that was halted on Wednesday night due to bad light. The American saved a match point at 5-4 down in the third set before managing to hold, break her opponent and then serve out to love for a 6-7 (5-7) 6-2 7-5 success. Venus, who lost the 2002 final to Serena, will next play Hungarian 29th seed Agnes Szavay. Fifth seed Jelena Jankovic had no such troubles in beating Magdalena Rybarikova of Slovakia 6-1 6-2, setting up a third-round clash with unseeded Austrian Jarmila Groth. Seventh-seeded Russian Svetlana Kuznetsova also advanced along with Danish 10th seed Caroline Wozniacki, but 13th seed Marion Bartoli of France made a surprise exit. The 2007 Wimbledon finalist lost 6-3 7-5 to Tathiana Garbin of Italy, who will next take on unseeded Virginie Razzano of France.

Jelena Dokic entered the 2009 French Open as an unseeded wild-card story, continuing a sensational comeback season after having reached the quarterfinals of the Australian Open earlier that year following years of personal turmoil and severe depression. 

Her second-round opponent was Russia’s **Elena Dementieva**, the tournament’s **4th seed** and the reigning Olympic gold medalist.

* **The Early Dominance:** Dokic started the match playing blistering, aggressive tennis reminiscent of her former top-4 form. She completely outplayed Dementieva in the opening set, taking it **6–2** in just 28 minutes. 
* **The Injury:** Early in the second set, Dokic suffered a severe lower back injury (later diagnosed as a torn back muscle) after hitting a shot. 
* **The Struggle and Retirement:** Visibly in excruciating pain, Dokic took a medical timeout and attempted to play on, but her movement was severely restricted. She broke down in tears on court as she realized she could no longer serve or stretch properly. 
* **The Result:** With Dementieva leading **4–3** in the second set, Dokic was forced to retire. The official scoreline was **Dementieva def. Dokic 2–6, 4–3 (ret.)**. 

It was a heartbreaking exit for Dokic, who was reduced to tears as she embraced Dementieva at the net. Dementieva was extremely sympathetic, offering warm words to Dokic as the Paris crowd gave the Australian a standing ovation.

---

### **2. How the Rest of the Top Women's Seeds Performed That Day**

May 28, 2009, featured second-round action from the bottom half of the women’s draw. While top contenders largely advanced safely, there were a few notable upsets.

#### **The Favorites Cruised:**
* **Serena Williams (No. 2 seed):** Serena produced a dominant performance, routing Spanish veteran Virginia Ruano Pascual **6–0, 6–3** in just 61 minutes.
* **Jelena Jankovic (No. 5 seed):** The former World No. 1 and 2008 semifinalist had a smooth outing, dismantling Slovakia's Magdalena Rybarikova **6–1, 6–2**.
* **Svetlana Kuznetsova (No. 7 seed):** The Russian—who would go on to win the French Open title two weeks later—defeated Kazakhstan’s Galina Voskoboeva **6–4, 6–2**.
* **Caroline Wozniacki (No. 10 seed):** The rising Danish star beat American veteran Jill Craybas **6–1, 6–4**.
* **Agnieszka Radwanska (No. 12 seed):** Comfortably dispatched Mariya Koryttseva **6–1, 6–4**.

#### **Key Upsets and Surprises:**
* **Marion Bartoli (No. 13 seed):** The biggest home disappointment came when French favorite Bartoli was shocked by Italian veteran Tathiana Garbin, losing **6–3, 7–5**.
* **Zheng Jie (No. 15 seed):** The semifinalist at Wimbledon the previous year was stunned by 16-year-old Portuguese prodigy Michelle Larcher de Brito in straight sets, **6–4, 6–3**.
* **Anabel Medina Garrigues (No. 18 seed):** The clay-court specialist was beaten by France's Virginie Razzano **6–2, 6–2**.
* **Kaia Kanepi (No. 19 seed):** Upset by Kazakh qualifier Yaroslava Shvedova, losing **6–4, 4–6, 6–2**.

### **Summary**
While major names like Serena Williams, Jelena Jankovic, and ultimate champion Svetlana Kuznetsova rolled smoothly into the third round, the day was emotionally overshadowed by Jelena Dokic’s painful back injury that cut short what looked to be a massive upset over 4th-seeded Elena Dementieva.
